products.superPrompt:
You are a sports-stationery designer. Produce the complete interior of a paper training log for first-time racers of a standardized 8-station indoor fitness race (eight 1 km runs, each followed by one workout station). The log records training; it never prescribes it.

BUYER AND JOB
First-time fitness racers training toward a spring 2027 event, and gym partners buying them a January gift. The format never changes, so splits are comparable week to week. The log holds every split, station personal best (PB) and "compromised run" (a run straight after a station), plus a calm race-day plan.

DELIVERABLES (same content, two builds)
A) KDP paperback interior: 6 x 9 in, no bleed, exactly 120 pages, inside (gutter) margin 0.75 in, other margins 0.5 in, black ink only (grayscale).
B) Printable PDF: US Letter 8.5 x 11 in and A4 210 x 297 mm, portrait, 0.5 in (13 mm) margins, plus a "print as needed" set (one week of pages, one station PB page, the race-day sheet).

PAGE LIST (KDP numbering)
1 Title: "[YOUR BRAND] Split & Station Log", subtitle "16 weeks of runs, stations and race-day splits", lines for name, race city, race date, target finish time.
2 How to use (max 150 words) plus plain definitions: run split, station time, transition time, compromised run, PB.
3 Disclaimer (verbatim, below).
4 Why I signed up: 5 prompts, division entered (blank).
5 Baseline: 1 km run plus each station with blank columns for distance/reps, load, time, date, notes.
6-13 Station PB pages in race order: Ski machine, Sled push, Sled pull, Burpee broad jumps, Rowing machine, Farmers carry, Sandbag lunges, Wall balls. Each: blank "my standard" box, PB ladder (date | time | load | notes | effort 1-5) x 12 rows, lined box "Cues in my own words" (no cues printed).
14-77 Sixteen weeks x 4 pages: (a) week grid, Mon-Sun rows; columns session type | planned | done (checkbox) | minutes | effort 1-10 | notes; week-focus box; 1-5 energy check. (b-d) three session pages: date, session type, warm-up notes, split table of 8 rows (run # | run time | station | station time | transition | running total), totals box, "felt strong" and "change next time" lines.
78-83 Compromised running log: date | station before | fresh 1 km | post-station 1 km | difference | notes, 14 rows per page.
84-86 Checkpoints for Weeks 0, 8 and 16 repeating page 5's grid plus a "change since last checkpoint" column.
87-88 Race-week checklist: gear, ticket and ID, travel, sleep notes, "my food and fluid plan" (blank lines only), wave time, event rules to check.
89-90 Race-day split sheet: target vs actual for 8 runs, 8 stations and transitions, running totals, large number boxes.
91-92 Post-race reflection: finish time, strongest and hardest segment, what I'd change, next goal.
93-94 Race history: date | city | division | finish time | notes, 10 rows each.
95-120 Notes: 5 mm dot grid.

DESIGN
Fonts: Oswald (headings, caps), Inter (body 10-11 pt), Space Mono (time fields). Palette "Chalk & Signal": Chalk #F7F7F5, Graphite #1E2328, Signal Orange #FF5A1F, Steel Blue #3A6EA5, Concrete #9AA3AB. KDP interior: Graphite and Concrete only; printable may use orange headers. Rules 0.5 pt, rows at least 0.3 in tall, time boxes pre-printed with ":".

CONTENT RULES
Original wording, grade 7-8 reading level, encouraging, factual. Never prescribe workouts, paces, loads, nutrition or recovery. No promises of faster times, fitness, weight loss or injury prevention. Never name any race series, organizer, sponsor, venue, equipment maker or apparel brand; use only the generic station names above.

DIFFERENTIATION
Plans and apps exist. This is the paper companion: split and station tracking, compromised-run comparison and a race-day sheet in one book, with no plan to follow.

DISCLAIMER (verbatim)
"This log is a record-keeping tool, not a training plan or medical advice. Talk to a qualified professional before starting or changing an exercise program. Not affiliated with or endorsed by any race organizer."

OUTPUT FORMAT
1) KDP table: page | title | elements | fields/columns | rows | layout notes. 2) Differences for the Letter/A4 printable. 3) Final text for pages 1-4, 87-88 and 91-92. 4) Repeat map of pages that duplicate one master.
Self-check, fixing failures before answering: [ ] exactly 120 KDP pages; [ ] grayscale interior; [ ] every split table has 8 runs and 8 stations in race order; [ ] no brand, organizer, sponsor or equipment names; [ ] no training, health or outcome claims; [ ] disclaimer verbatim.

You are a spreadsheet designer and printable-stationery designer. Produce a complete race-day pacing kit for first-time racers of a standardized 8-station indoor fitness race (eight 1 km runs, each followed by one workout station). The kit does arithmetic on the racer's own numbers; it never tells them how fast to go.

BUYER AND JOB
First-time racers 2-6 weeks out. They have a target finish time and some practice times and want a concrete split plan, a card to carry and a checklist that keeps race week calm. Book bonuses and apps exist; this is a cheap, single-purpose, race-week kit that complements them.

PART 1: GOOGLE SHEETS FILE (give every tab, cell, label, formula, number format, validation and protected range)
Tab "Start Here": title, 6-step instructions (make a copy, fill yellow cells, print the strip), the disclaimer.
Tab "My Times":
- A2 "Target finish time", B2 input, format [h]:mm:ss. A3 "Scale factor", B3 =IF(D23=0,"",B2/D23), format 0.000. C2 =IF(B3="","",IF(ROUND((G21-B2)*86400,0)=0,"Adds up","Check inputs")).
- Row 5 headers: # | Segment | Type | My practice time | Share | Target time | Target clock at end | vs practice.
- Rows 6-21, 16 segments in order: Run 1, Ski machine, Run 2, Sled push, Run 3, Sled pull, Run 4, Burpee broad jumps, Run 5, Rowing machine, Run 6, Farmers carry, Run 7, Sandbag lunges, Run 8, Wall balls. Row 22 "Transitions (total)". D23 =SUM(D6:D22).
- E6 =IF($B$3="","",D6/$D$23) (percent); F6 =IF($B$3="","",D6*$B$3) (m:ss); G6 =IF($B$3="","",SUM($F$6:F6)+$F$22/16*(ROW()-5)) ([h]:mm:ss); H6 =IF($B$3="","",IF(F6>=D6,"+","-")&TEXT(ABS(F6-D6),"m:ss")). Fill E6:H6 down to row 21. F22 =IF($B$3="","",D22*$B$3).
- Validation on B2 and D6:D22: duration greater than 0:00:00. Inputs filled #FFF4C2. Grey italic example inputs labelled "EXAMPLE: replace with your own times".
Tab "Wrist Card": print-ready block pulling segment names, target times and clock from "My Times" (show formulas); two columns (runs | stations); Space Mono 12 pt; print setup landscape, fit to width, no gridlines.
Tab "Race-Day Actuals": same 16 segments plus transitions; target | actual (input) | difference (signed m:ss) | running total; total row.
Tab "Checklist": checkboxes; sections Clothing and shoes, Ticket/ID, Bag, Before the start, "My food and drink plan (what / when)" as blank rows only, After the finish, "Event rules to check" (gloves, headphones, bag drop).

PART 2: PRINTABLE PDF (US Letter and A4 versions)
Page 1 Wrist strips 10 x 2 in (A4: 265 x 48 mm), 4 per landscape page, two rows of 8 boxes (top Run 1-8, bottom the stations in order), blank time lines, dashed cut lines.
Page 2 Mini pace cards 3.5 x 2 in (A4: 85 x 55 mm), 10 per portrait page, 16 segments with blank target lines.
Page 3 One-page race-week checklist matching the tab.
Page 4 "How to fill in your strip" with a worked example marked EXAMPLE, plus the disclaimer.

DESIGN
Palette "Chalk & Signal": Chalk #F7F7F5, Graphite #1E2328, Signal Orange #FF5A1F, Steel Blue #3A6EA5, Concrete #9AA3AB. Fonts: Oswald headings, Inter body, Space Mono for times. Header rows Graphite with Chalk text; only input cells yellow.

CONTENT RULES
Original wording, grade 7 reading level. No pacing, training, nutrition, hydration or medical advice; no promises about finish times. Never name any race series, organizer, sponsor, equipment maker or apparel brand; generic station names only.

DISCLAIMER (verbatim): "This kit only does arithmetic on the times you enter. It is not coaching, nutrition or medical advice. Not affiliated with or endorsed by any race organizer."

OUTPUT FORMAT
Tab by tab, a cell table (cell | content or formula | format). Then the PDF page by page: dimensions, grid and every label.
Self-check, fixing failures before answering: [ ] with the example inputs, G21 equals B2 and C2 reads "Adds up"; [ ] every formula points at the right rows; [ ] 8 runs and 8 stations in race order everywhere; [ ] Letter and A4 sizes both given; [ ] no brand names; [ ] no advice or outcome claims.

asymmetry.badBetIf: KDP journals are crowded and Amazon rarely surfaces a new journal with no reviews or outside traffic, so if you cannot drive Pinterest or video traffic it may sit unseen. Low cash risk, but slow feedback; moderately asymmetric.
